title: P46 (Chester Beatty II): Hebrews 13:3-1 Corinthians 1:3 (fols. 37r-38r)
source: P46 (Chester Beatty Biblical Papyrus II, Chester Beatty Library, Dublin): photographs as published in the INTF New Testament Virtual Manuscript Room; Greek from the INTF NTVMR transcription of P46; English from the King James Version
description: Hebrews 13:3-1 Corinthians 1:3 in P46, the papyrus codex of Paul's letters copied around 200: fols. 37r-38r, each page with its photograph, the Greek transcription and the King James Version.
introduction:
P46 is a papyrus codex of the letters of Paul copied in Egypt around 200, the oldest surviving collection of Paul's letters. 86 of its 104 leaves survive: 56 in the Chester Beatty Library, Dublin (Biblical Papyrus II, published by Frederic Kenyon in 1934-1937) and 30 in the University of Michigan Library, Ann Arbor (P.Mich. inv. 6238, published by Henry Sanders in 1935). The letters run in the order Romans, Hebrews, 1 and 2 Corinthians, Ephesians, Galatians, Philippians, Colossians and 1 Thessalonians; the first seven leaves (Romans 1:1-5:17) and the end of the book are lost. Hebrews standing after Romans, and the doxology of Romans (16:25-27) standing after 15:33, are among its best-known features.

Each section below is one page side: the holding library's photograph, the NTVMR diplomatic transcription line by line, and the King James Version of every verse that has text on the page. The lower lines of many leaves are lost; the transcribers' restorations are in square brackets.

This entry covers fols. 37r-38r (Hebrews 13:3-1 Corinthians 1:3).
translator_notes: Greek: the NTVMR diplomatic transcription, line by line as on the papyrus. Square brackets enclose letters that are lost or illegible and were supplied by the transcribers; a dot under a letter marks it as uncertain; [...] marks a gap. Nomina sacra and numerals keep the scribe's overline. Spelling is the scribe's (no accents or breathings). Words broken at a line end stay broken as on the papyrus. Corrections are not shown: the text is the first hand.

English: the King James Version (1611), whole verses, for every verse that has text on the page. A verse that begins on one page and ends on the next is given in full on both. The KJV translates a later form of the Greek text, so its wording does not always match the papyrus; material differences (such as verses the papyrus does not have) are noted in the section.

translation.text: <sup>13:3</sup>Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them; and them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body. <sup>4</sup>Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge. <sup>5</sup>Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee. <sup>6</sup>So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me. <sup>7</sup>Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation. <sup>8</sup>Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever. <sup>9</sup>Be not carried about with divers and strange doctrines. For it is a good thing that the heart be established with grace; not with meats, which have not profited them that have been occupied therein. <sup>10</sup>We have an altar, where of they have no right to eat which serve the tabernacle. <sup>11</sup>For the bodies of those beasts, whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sin, are burned without the camp.

translation.text: <sup>13:12</sup>Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate. <sup>13</sup>Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach. <sup>14</sup>For here have we no continuing city, but we seek one to come. <sup>15</sup>By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name. <sup>16</sup>But to do good and to communicate forget not: for with such sacrifices God is well pleased. <sup>17</sup>Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you. <sup>18</sup>Pray for us: for we trust we have a good conscience, in all things willing to live honestly. <sup>19</sup>But I beseech you the rather to do this, that I may be restored to you the sooner. <sup>20</sup>Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant,

translation.text: <sup>13:20</sup>Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant, <sup>21</sup>Make you perfect in every good work to do his will, working in you that which is wellpleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ; to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen. <sup>22</sup>And I beseech you, brethren, suffer the word of exhortation: for I have written a letter unto you in few words. <sup>23</sup>Know ye that our brother Timothy is set at liberty; with whom, if he come shortly, I will see you. <sup>24</sup>Salute all them that have the rule over you, and all the saints. They of Italy salute you. <sup>25</sup>Grace be with you all. Amen. <sup>1 Corinthians 1:1</sup>Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother, <sup>2</sup>Unto the church of God which is at Corinth, to them that are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, with all that in every place call upon the name of Jesus Christ our Lord, both theirs and ours: <sup>3</sup>Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
